text: Pecorino is deliberately made attractive to the cheese fly: it is lightly pressed, briefly brined and its rind pierced and oiled, so that Piophila casei lays its eggs inside. The larvae break down the paste, which turns soft to spreadably creamy with a strong, penetrating, piquant taste.

steps.note: The cheese is pressed into cylinders of mostly 2–4 kg.
The cheese is put briefly into brine, so the salt does not deter the fly.
Holes are pierced into the rind, with a drop of oil in each, so the fly lays its eggs inside.
The paste is broken down by the larvae, with few turnings, from late spring to autumn.
